Combustor outlet temperatures in modern gas turbine engines can exceed the blade and disk material limits by 600 °F or more.
Internal convective cooling is inadequate in many blade locations, and both internal and film cooling approaches can lead to significant performance penalties in the engine.
Micro Cooling Concepts, Inc. has developed a turbine blade cooling concept that uses microtextured impingement surfaces to enhance the cooling capability.
The microtextured surfaces significantly increase the cooling capability of the impinging flow, compared to conventional untextured surfaces.
The microtextured surface cooling concept can be combined with microchannel cooling and external film cooling to tailor the cooling capability per the external heating profile.
The cooling system can be optimized to minimize impact on engine performance.
Potential applications include turbine engine development, military and commercial aircraft, power generation plants, electronics, industrial processes, automotive, and lasers.
The Phase II objective is to evaluate the suitability of high-temperature materials (e.g., from the Inconel or HAYNES series) for this application.
The microtextured surface cooling concept can enable higher combustion temperatures with lower engine penalties.
The microtextured surface cooling concept can enable tailored cooling capability to optimize the cooling system.
The microtextured surface cooling concept is part of the Versatile Affordable Advanced Turbine Engine (VAATE) initiative.
Micro Cooling Concepts, Inc. is the company developing the microtextured surface cooling concept.
The paper was published as a NASA Technical Memorandum (NASA/TM—2014-218497).
